title: Bandwidth sensitivity and RDD robustness checks

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Method: Sharp Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD) around the Russell reconstitution cutoff (running _var = 0.5).  
Why: Index assignment is a deterministic, discontinuous rule—firms with rank > 0.5 enter the Russell 2000 (treated); those ≤ 0.5 remain in the Russell 1000 (control). Close to the cutoff, assignment is as-good-as random, so comparing outcomes on either side identifies the causal effect of index membership.  

Key assumptions  
• Continuity: Potential outcomes and covariates evolve smoothly in running_var at the cutoff; any jump in y is attributable to treatment.  
• No precise manipulation: Firms cannot perfectly sort around the 0.5 threshold at the reconstitution date.  

Robustness checks required  
• Bandwidth choice (narrow vs. wide).  
• Polynomial order (local linear vs. quadratic).  
• Placebo cutoffs (e.g., 0.30 and 0.70) to verify no spurious jumps away from the true threshold.  


## 2. R Code
```r
#######################################################################
# Russell 1000/2000 RDD – institutional ownership
#######################################################################

# 0. Packages ----------------------------------------------------------
required <- c("readr", "dplyr", "ggplot2", "rdrobust")
invisible(lapply(required, function(p) if (!requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)) install.packages(p)))
library(readr); library(dplyr); library(ggplot2); library(rdrobust)

# 1. Read data ---------------------------------------------------------
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s29_data.csv"
df   <- read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE)

# 2. Main RDD estimate (local‐linear, MSE-optimal bandwidth) ----------
cutoff <- 0.5
main_rd <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = cutoff, p = 1)

cat("Main local‐linear RDD estimate (bandwidth h =", round(main_rd$bws[1,1],4),")\n")
print(summary(main_rd))

# Extract point estimate and 95% CI
est  <- main_rd$coef[1]
ci_l <- main_rd$ci[1,1]; ci_u <- main_rd$ci[1,2]
cat("\nEstimated treatment effect:", round(est,4),
    "| 95% CI [", round(ci_l,4), ",", round(ci_u,4), "]\n\n")

# 3. Bandwidth sensitivity --------------------------------------------
band_seq <- c(0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20)      # absolute bandwidths around cutoff
band_results <- lapply(band_seq, function(h){
  tmp <- rdrobust(df$y, df$running_var, c = cutoff, h = h, p = 1, kernel = "triangular")
  data.frame(bw = h,
             coef = tmp$coef[1],
             se   = tmp$se[1],
             ci_l = tmp$ci[1,1],
             ci_u = tmp$ci[1,2])
}) %>% bind_rows()

cat("Bandwidth‐sensitivity (local‐linear):\n")
print(band_results)

# 4. Polynomial order sensitivity -------------------------------------
lin  <- rdrobust(df$y, df$running_var, c = cutoff, p = 1)  # already computed
quad <- rdrobust(df$y, df$running_var, c = cutoff, p = 2)

cat("\nPolynomial order sensitivity:\n")
poly_tbl <- data.frame(order = c("Linear","Quadratic"),
                       coef  = c(lin$coef[1], quad$coef[1]),
                       se    = c(lin$se[1],   quad$se[1]),
                       ci_l  = c(lin$ci[1,1], quad$ci[1,1]),
                       ci_u  = c(lin$ci[1,2], quad$ci[1,2]))
print(poly_tbl)

# 5. Placebo cutoffs ---------------------------------------------------
placebo_cuts <- c(0.30, 0.70)
placebo_out  <- lapply(placebo_cuts, function(cut){
  tmp <- rdrobust(df$y, df$running_var, c = cut, p = 1)
  data.frame(cutoff = cut,
             coef   = tmp$coef[1],
             se     = tmp$se[1],
             ci_l   = tmp$ci[1,1],
             ci_u   = tmp$ci[1,2])
}) %>% bind_rows()

cat("\nPlacebo‐cutoff tests (should be ≈0):\n")
print(placebo_out)

# 6. Simple RD plot ----------------------------------------------------
ggplot(df %>% filter(abs(running_var - cutoff) <= 0.25),
       aes(x = running_var, y = y, color = treated)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = cutoff, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_smooth(data = df, method = "lm",
              formula = y ~ poly(running_var,1), se = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "RDD: Institutional ownership around Russell cutoff",
       x = "Normalized market‐cap rank", y = "Institutional ownership") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Sign: Positive. Moving from the bottom of the Russell 1000 to the top of the Russell 2000 raises index fund demand, so institutional ownership should jump upward at the cutoff.  

Magnitude: Prior literature (e.g., Chang, Hong & Liskovich 2015) finds increases of roughly 3–6 percentage points in institutional ownership. Given the sample size (n ≈ 600) and that we are focusing on firms very near the threshold, expect an estimated jump of about +0.04 to +0.06 (4–6 p.p.).  

Robustness checks should show the estimate remains positive and statistically significant across reasonable bandwidths and polynomial orders, while placebo cutoffs yield coefficients near zero, supporting the validity of the design.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Sharp RDD — rank cutoff; rdrobust with CCT bandwidth; donut-hole robustness; placebo cutoffs
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Russell 2000 membership increases institutional ownership; robust to bandwidth choice
